walkthroughs.body_html:
Fields & Their Consequences — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fields & Their Consequences brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fields & Their Consequences.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, the gravitational force between them is:
options: Halved
Doubled
Quartered
Quadrupled

mcqs.q: Gravitational potential at infinity is taken to be:
options: Infinite
Maximum positive
Zero
Negative

mcqs.q: If the distance between two masses doubles, what happens to the gravitational force between them?
options: It quarters — gravitational force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
It halves — gravitational force is inversely proportional to distance.

mcqs.q: Why is gravitational potential energy near a planet treated as negative?
options: Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity does negative work.
Because the zero is defined at infinity; objects bound to the planet have lower (negative) potential energy than at infinity.
Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
Gravitational potential energy is negative because gravity always points downwards.

mcqs.q: What does the spacing of field lines on a diagram indicate?
options: Wider spacing means a stronger field because the lines have more room to act.
Field lines are equally important regardless of spacing — only the arrows matter.
The strength of the field — closer lines mean a stronger field.
It doubles — more distance means more space for gravity to act through.
